# 🎥 Criminal Activity Detection Model Card

## Overview
A deep learning–based **video classification system** that labels short clips as **Normal** or **Suspicious**. The model is trained on the UCF-Crime dataset and is designed for **surveillance analysis**, supporting both offline video and real-time streams.

The pipeline combines **spatial feature extraction (CNN)** with **temporal modeling (RNN + attention)** to capture motion patterns indicative of anomalous behavior.

---

## Intended Use

### ✅ Primary Use Cases
- Surveillance monitoring (CCTV analysis)
- Smart city safety systems
- Automated alerting for abnormal activities
- Pre-screening large volumes of video footage

### ⚠️ Limitations / Out-of-Scope
- Not suitable for legal or forensic decision-making without human review  
- Not designed for identifying specific individuals or faces  
- Performance may degrade on:
  - Low-light footage  
  - Non-surveillance camera angles  
  - Domains outside training distribution  

---

## Model Architecture

```
Input video (2 sec clip, 16 frames)
        ↓
ResNet50 (ImageNet pretrained, frozen)
        ↓
Frame embeddings (16 × 2048)
        ↓
LayerNorm → Dense(256) → Dropout(0.4)
        ↓
Bidirectional GRU (64 units)
        ↓
Temporal Attention Layer
        ↓
Dense(64) → Dropout(0.6)
        ↓
Sigmoid Output → P(suspicious)
```

### Key Design Choices
- **Frozen CNN backbone** → avoids overfitting on limited data  
- **Bidirectional GRU** → captures forward & backward temporal context  
- **Attention layer** → focuses on important frames within a clip  

---

## Training Details

| Parameter | Value |
|----------|------|
| Framework | TensorFlow / Keras |
| Backbone | ResNet50 (frozen) |
| Sequence length | 16 frames |
| Clip duration | ~2 seconds |
| Batch size | 32 |
| Epochs | ~19 (early stopped) |
| Optimizer | Adam (clipnorm=1.0) |
| Loss | Focal Loss (α=0.60, γ=2.0) |
| LR schedule | ReduceLROnPlateau |
| Early stopping | Based on validation AUC |

### Training Strategy
- Feature extraction performed once and cached  
- Stratified **video-level splits** to prevent leakage  
- Threshold tuned using **macro-F1**, not class-specific metrics  

---

## Dataset

### Source
- UCF-Crime dataset  
- ~1,950 surveillance videos  

### Classes
- **Suspicious (13 categories):** Abuse, Arrest, Arson, Assault, Burglary, Explosion, Fighting, Road Accidents, Robbery, Shooting, Shoplifting, Stealing, Vandalism  
- **Normal:** Non-criminal surveillance footage  

### Splits

| Split | Clips | Normal | Suspicious |
|------|------|--------|------------|
| Train | 1,328 | 51.2% | 48.8% |
| Val | 332 | 51.2% | 48.8% |
| Test | 290 | 51.7% | 48.3% |

---

## Performance

| Metric | Score |
|-------|------|
| Accuracy | 90.3% |
| AUC-ROC | 0.930 |
| Macro F1 | 0.903 |

### Class-wise Performance

| Class | Precision | Recall |
|------|----------|--------|
| Normal | 89.6% | 92.0% |
| Suspicious | 91.2% | 88.6% |

### Errors
- False Positives: 12 / 150  
- False Negatives: 16 / 140  

---

## Inference

### Supported Inputs
- Video files (MP4, AVI, etc.)
- Live streams (Webcam, RTSP, RTMP)

### Method
- Sliding window over video stream  
- Default **50% overlap** to avoid missing events  

### Performance
- ~135 ms per 2-second clip (T4 GPU)  
- Real-time capable with batching and warm-up  

---

## Known Issues & Fixes

| Issue | Resolution |
|------|-----------|
| Class imbalance bias | Focal Loss tuning |
| Overfitting | Frozen backbone |
| Slow preprocessing | Batched GPU feature extraction |
| Threshold bias | Macro-F1 optimization |
| Serialization errors | Keras serializable registration |
| Training interruptions | Checkpoint + resume support |
| Feature extraction crashes | Incremental checkpointing |
| Dataset path issues | Auto-discovery logic |
| Data leakage risk | Video-level splitting |

---

## Ethical Considerations

- **False alarms** may lead to unnecessary alerts or interventions  
- **Missed detections** could fail to flag real incidents  
- Model should always be used **with human oversight**  
- Avoid deployment in sensitive contexts without bias evaluation  

---

## Future Improvements

- Fine-tuning backbone with regularization  
- Multi-class classification (crime type prediction)  
- Transformer-based temporal modeling  
- Edge deployment optimization (TensorRT / ONNX)  
- Domain adaptation for real-world CCTV environments  

EOF

models.description:
## Overview
A video-based binary classifier that labels any clip as **Normal** or **Suspicious**. Trained end-to-end on the [UCF-Crime dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/minmints/ufc-crime-full-dataset) — 1,950 annotated surveillance videos across 13 crime categories (Abuse, Arrest, Arson, Assault, Burglary, Explosion, Fighting, Road Accidents, Robbery, Shooting, Shoplifting, Stealing, Vandalism) plus matched normal footage.

---

## Architecture

```
Raw video
   ↓
ResNet50 (frozen, ImageNet)       ← feature extractor, 25M params
   ↓  16 frames × 2048-dim vectors
LayerNorm + Dense(256) + Dropout(0.4)
   ↓
Bidirectional GRU (64 units)      ← temporal modelling
   ↓
Temporal Attention                ← learned frame weighting
   ↓
Dense(64) + Dropout(0.6)
   ↓
Sigmoid → P(suspicious)
```

**Head parameters:** 660,738 (2.52 MB)
**Backbone:** Frozen ResNet50 — features extracted once and cached, not retrained

---

## Training Details

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Framework | TensorFlow 2.19.0 / Keras 3 |
| GPU | 2× Tesla T4 (Kaggle) |
| Loss | Focal Loss (α=0.60, γ=2.0) |
| Optimiser | Adam + gradient clipping (clipnorm=1.0) |
| LR schedule | ReduceLROnPlateau on val_AUC, min 1e-5 |
| Early stopping | Patience 6 on val_AUC, restore best weights |
| Epochs run | 19 (best at epoch 13) |
| Batch size | 32 |
| Sequence length | 16 frames per 2-second clip |
| Threshold | 0.325 (macro-F1 tuned on validation set) |

---

## Dataset Splits

| Split | Clips | Normal | Suspicious |
|---|---|---|---|
| Train | 1,328 | 680 (51.2%) | 648 (48.8%) |
| Val | 332 | 170 (51.2%) | 162 (48.8%) |
| Test | 290 | 150 (51.7%) | 140 (48.3%) |

Splits are at **video level** — no frame-level leakage between train and val. Val is a stratified 20% carve-out of the training pool.

---

## Results

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Test accuracy | 90.3% |
| Test AUC-ROC | 0.930 |
| Macro F1 | 0.903 |
| Normal precision / recall | 89.6% / 92.0% |
| Suspicious precision / recall | 91.2% / 88.6% |
| False alarms (FP) | 12 / 150 normal clips |
| Misses (FN) | 16 / 140 suspicious clips |

---

## Inference

Supports both **recorded video** and **live streams** (webcam, RTSP, RTMP) via a sliding window with configurable overlap:

```python
model = tf.keras.models.load_model('best_model.keras')
# No custom_objects needed — @register_keras_serializable handles it
```

**Latency:** ~135 ms per 2-second window on T4 GPU (after tf.function warm-up)
**Overlap:** 50% default — events spanning clip boundaries are always fully captured

---

## Fixes Applied Across Versions

| Issue | Fix |
|---|---|
| Class weight collapse (v1) | Focal Loss α=0.60 |
| Backbone overfitting | ResNet50 frozen throughout |
| Slow extraction | Batched GPU extraction (~8× faster) |
| Threshold bias | Macro-F1 tuning instead of suspicious-only F1 |
| Custom class serialisation | `@register_keras_serializable` |
| Training resume after crash | Epoch history + weight checkpoint |
| Feature extraction resume | Incremental partial `.npz` checkpoint every 200 clips |
| Dataset path resolution | BFS auto-discovery + 5-layout fallback |
| Leakage | Video-level splits confirmed |

---

## Model Details

### Overview  
This model is a **LoRA fine-tuned adapter** built on top of the Nemotron-3 Nano 30B (BF16) base model. It is optimized for reasoning tasks, with a focus on structured outputs where the final answer is enclosed in `\boxed{}`.

---

### Base Model  
- Model: Nemotron-3 Nano 30B  
- Precision: bfloat16 (BF16)  
- Framework: Hugging Face Transformers (`trust_remote_code=True`)  
- Device: Single GPU  

---

### Training Methodology  
- Fine-tuning approach: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) using LoRA  
- Trainer: SFTTrainer from TRL (Supervised Fine-Tuning)  
- Objective: Causal Language Modeling in chat format  

---

### LoRA Configuration  
- Rank (r): fixed to satisfy evaluation constraints  
- Alpha: aligned with rank  
- Dropout: applied for regularization  
- Bias: none  
- Target modules:  
  - `in_proj`  
  - `x_proj`  
  - `dt_proj`  
  - `out_proj`  

This setup is designed to balance memory efficiency and model expressiveness.

---

### Dataset  
- Source: Nemotron reasoning dataset (`train.csv`)  
- Sampling: subset sampling applied for training efficiency  
- Format: converted into chat-style instruction-response pairs  
- Special instruction:  
  - The model is explicitly guided to output final answers inside `\boxed{}`  
  - Training assumes responses may include reasoning steps followed by the final answer  

---

### Input Formatting  
Each example is transformed into a structured conversation:

- **User message**:  
  - Original problem prompt  
  - Additional instruction to format the final answer inside `\boxed{}`  

- **Assistant message**:  
  - Ground truth response (expected to include reasoning and final answer)  

---

### Training Configuration  
- Epochs: configurable  
- Batch size: configurable  
- Gradient accumulation: used to simulate larger effective batch size  
- Learning rate: configurable  
- Scheduler: cosine decay  
- Warmup: applied at the beginning of training  
- Sequence length: extended to support reasoning tasks  
- Gradient clipping: enabled  

---

### Memory & Optimization Techniques  
- Gradient checkpointing enabled for memory efficiency  
- Custom RMSNorm fallback implementation to ensure stability  
- Triton backend patched for compatibility with the execution environment  
- CUDA memory optimization enabled via expandable segments  

---

### Output  
- Output type: LoRA adapter (base model weights remain frozen)  
- Saved components:  
  - Adapter weights  
  - Tokenizer configuration  
- Output directory: runtime-defined  

---

### Notes & Limitations  
- Model performance depends on the presence of reasoning steps in training data  
- Only adapter layers are trainable; base model is not updated  
- Environment-specific patches are required for stable execution  
- Dependency mismatches may exist but do not prevent training

# Cielo Adaptive Core: Inteligência de Preferências e Raciocínio Computacional
> **Candidato:** Prof. Dr. João Pedro Pereira Passos| **r – IA, Chatbot e Automatização (Inova Talentos)
> **Stack Principal:** NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Nano 30B | vLLM | QLoRA | Pydantic

## 1. Sumário Executivo
O **Cielo Adaptive Core** é uma arquitetura de IA conversacional de alto desempenho desenhada para o ecossistema de adquirência da Cielo. Ao contrário de chatbots convencionais, esta solução utiliza o modelo **NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Nano-30B** com *Thinking Budget* para processar intenções de negócio complexas, priorizando a retenção de lojistas e a conversão de produtos financeiros (TPV) com latência inferior a 300ms.

---

## 2. Definição de Canais e Justificativa
A estratégia multicanal foca na ubiquidade e na jornada do lojista:

| Canal | Justificativa Técnica e de Negócio |
| :--- | :--- |
| **WhatsApp Business** | Baixa fricção, alta penetração e ideal para notificações proativas de faturamento. |
| **App Cielo** | Ambiente seguro para transações críticas, permitindo UI rica e autenticação MFA. |
| **API B2B (Headless)** | Permite que grandes varejistas integrem a inteligência da Cielo nos seus próprios ERPs. |

---

## 3. Modelagem de Intents (Reasoning Flows)
A solução utiliza a técnica de **Chain-of-Thought (CoT)** para garantir que a IA "pense" antes de responder.

### 3.1 Antecipação de Recebíveis
- **Input:** "Preciso de capital de giro hoje."
- **Reasoning:** Identifica faturamento acumulado -> Avalia Score de Risco -> Seleciona taxa promocional.
- **Output:** Oferta personalizada com botão de contratação imediata.

### 3.2 Suporte Técnico (Terminais LIO)
- **Input:** "Erro 05 na maquininha."
- **Reasoning:** Consulta base de conhecimento técnica -> Identifica falha de comunicação de rede.
- **Output:** Passo a passo de resolução e auto-diagnóstico remoto.

### 3.3 Gestão de Taxas e Retenção
- **Input:** "Quero cancelar, a concorrência ofereceu taxa menor."
- **Reasoning:** Calcula LTV (Lifetime Value) -> Aplica Matriz de Retenção -> Oferece isenção de aluguel.
- **Output:** Negociação ativa baseada em dados reais de lucro.

---

## 4. Arquitetura Técnica e Escalabilidade
A arquitetura foi desenhada seguindo princípios de **Cloud Native** e **MLOps**.

### 4.1 O Motor de Inferência (NVIDIA Stack)
- **Modelo:** `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16`.
- **Otimização:** Quantização **4-bit NF4** via *bitsandbytes* para viabilidade em GPUs T4/L4.
- **Serving:** Uso de **vLLM** com *PagedAttention* para suportar múltiplos lojistas simultâneos sem degradação de performance.

### 4.2 Segurança e Compliance (LGPD)
- **Validação de Output:** Framework **Pydantic** para garantir que o modelo nunca vaze dados sensíveis (PII) e responda em formatos JSON estritos.
- **Sandbox:** O modelo opera isolado, comunicando com os sistemas core da Cielo apenas através de camadas de integração validadas.

---

## 5. Estratégia de Monitoramento e Evolução
- **Observabilidade:** Métricas via **Prometheus/Grafana** monitorando o AHT (Average Handle Time) e a taxa de conversão por intent.
- **Melhoria Contínua:** Implementação de **DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)** para alinhar o modelo com os melhores atendentes da Cielo sem a complexidade do RLHF tradicional.

---

## 6. Framework do Modelo (Technical Specs)
```yaml
Framework:
  Inference: vLLM / Hugging Face Transformers
  Fine-Tuning: QLoRA (Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning)
  Alignment: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)
  Security: Pydantic Structured Outputs
  Latency_Target: < 300ms/token
  License_Compliance: CC BY 4.0 (NVIDIA Requirement)

instances.overview:
Bem-vindo ao repositório oficial do CHATCIELO, um sistema de Machine Learning de missão crítica projetado para a Cielo Brasil.

Este projeto implementa um modelo de Pairwise Preference Ranking (inspirado no SOTA do Kaggle LMSYS) para personalizar o atendimento a lojistas, adaptando respostas de LLMs com base no perfil do usuário (MEI, Varejo, Corporate) e garantindo uma experiência conversacional de alta conversão e baixo churn.
instances.usage:
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, BitsAndBytesConfig
from schema import CieloResponse # Importa o contrato de dados acima

# 1. Carregamento Otimizado (Ambiente Kaggle/Produção)
model_id = "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16"

bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
    load_in_4bit=True,
    bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4"
)

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_id,
    quantization_config=bnb_config,
    device_map="auto",
    trust_remote_code=True
)

# 2. Simulação de Contexto (Feature Store Mock)
contexto_lojista = {
    "nome": "Mercado do João",
    "segmento": "Varejo Alimentos",
    "faturamento_mes": 45000.00,
    "maquina_ativa": "Cielo LIO",
    "churn_score": 0.8 # Alto risco
}

prompt_sistema = f"""
Você é o Cielo Adaptive Core. Use o modo /think para analisar os dados do lojista:
{contexto_lojista}
Responda sempre em formato JSON seguindo o esquema CieloResponse.
Priorize retenção e oferta de produtos se o sentimento for crítico.
"""

# 3. Execução de Inferência
pergunta_usuario = "Vou cancelar minha conta. A taxa da concorrência está 0.5% menor."

inputs = tokenizer(f"{prompt_sistema}\nUsuário: {pergunta_usuario}", return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=512)
res_text = tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True)

print(res_text)

## Model Description
This model is a YOLOv8n detector trained for thermal imagery with 3 classes: `Person`, `Car`, and `OtherVehicle`.

It is designed for lightweight, real-time inference in surveillance, robotics, and edge AI workflows.

Training was performed on the merged thermal dataset below, using Ultralytics YOLO and a 100-epoch setup.  
For full training details, preprocessing, and reproducibility, see the linked Kaggle notebook.

## Model Instance: `best.pt`

### Overview
- Framework: PyTorch / Ultralytics YOLOv8
- Task: Thermal object detection
- Classes:
  - `0: Person`
  - `1: Car`
  - `2: OtherVehicle`
- Recommended use: Real-time thermal detection baseline and fine-tuning starting point

### Example Usage
```python
!pip -q install ultralytics

from ultralytics import YOLO

# Update this path based on your Kaggle model mount location
model = YOLO("/kaggle/input/yolov8n-thermal/.../best.pt")

results = model.predict(
    source="/kaggle/input/thermal-car-person-othervehicle/images/test",
    imgsz=640,
    conf=0.25
